meta.method: Bottom-up clustering of 524 free-form problem tags, then merge/split/rename to 85%+ confidence per category

categories.tagline: Children dismissed, labelled, hit, or left to face the worst alone
categories.turnsInto: Child development, play therapy, progressive education, parenting coaching, youth advocacy

placemakes.label: Kids being talked at instead of talked to
placemakes.example: Like Fred Rogers airing a full minute of silence on television because he believed children deserved time to think about who loved them

placemakes.label: Children written off before anyone gives them a real chance
placemakes.example: Like Maria Montessori taking children from asylums labelled uneducable, designing tactile materials, and watching them pass standard Italian public school exams

placemakes.label: Children facing the worst moments of history with no adult beside them
placemakes.example: Like Janusz Korczak refusing offers to escape the Warsaw Ghetto, reportedly saying 'You do not leave children at a time like this,' then walking with 192 orphans to the Umschlagplatz

placemakes.label: Students not learning because nobody in the building actually likes them
placemakes.example: Like Rita Pierson grounding her whole case on one line: 'No significant learning can occur without a significant relationship'

placemakes.label: Children being pushed into a life their parents chose for them
placemakes.example: Like Andre Agassi being forced into tennis at age three by his father despite hating the sport, spending years in rebellion before finding his own relationship with the game

categories.tagline: People whose voice was taken, suppressed, or erased before they could use it
categories.turnsInto: Advocacy, voice coaching, expressive arts, storytelling workshops, memoir facilitation, identity work

placemakes.label: Childhood trauma stealing your ability to speak
placemakes.example: Like Maya Angelou going mute for nearly five years at age eight after being raped, until a family friend coaxed her out of silence by asking her to read poetry aloud

placemakes.label: Doing the work and someone else getting the credit
placemakes.example: Like Rosalind Franklin's X-ray crystallography data being used by Watson and Crick to crack DNA's structure without acknowledging her contribution

placemakes.label: Speaking the truth and losing your community for it
placemakes.example: Like Miriam Makeba testifying at the UN for an arms embargo on South Africa, then having her citizenship revoked, leaving her stateless for nearly 30 years

placemakes.label: Being forced to hide who you really are just to be accepted
placemakes.example: Like Audre Lorde publishing her self-description 'Black, lesbian, feminist, socialist, mother, warrior, poet' repeatedly, refusing to be listed in a narrower set of identities

placemakes.label: Carrying shame in silence because nobody models speaking about it
placemakes.example: Like Oprah Winfrey, molested as a child and pregnant at 14, turning that trauma into radical honesty on television and modelling vulnerability for millions

placemakes.label: Being used as inspiration for a struggle you didn't choose
placemakes.example: Like Stella Young coining 'inspiration porn' to name the practice of turning disabled people into motivational posters for people who can walk

categories.tagline: Physical suffering that nobody names, treats, or believes is real
categories.turnsInto: Health coaching, chronic illness support, somatic therapy, end-of-life care, pain advocacy

placemakes.label: A body in constant pain with no way to tell anyone what it feels like
placemakes.example: Like Frida Kahlo, whose bus accident at 18 broke her spine in three places and her right leg in eleven, painting from a mirror above her hospital bed for the rest of her life

placemakes.label: People dying in pain because the building they're in wasn't designed for dying
placemakes.example: Like Cicely Saunders introducing the concept of total pain, arguing opioid dosing had to be anticipatory rather than waiting for the patient to beg, then dying in her own hospice using the protocols she designed

placemakes.label: Poor people dying of treatable diseases because someone decided they weren't worth treating
placemakes.example: Like Paul Farmer walking eight hours to reach one patient because he argued the rural poor deserved the same treatment standards as patients at Harvard hospitals

placemakes.label: Burnout being treated as a badge of honour until your body forces you to stop
placemakes.example: Like Arianna Huffington collapsing from exhaustion and breaking her cheekbone on her desk, then spending years building Thrive Global to change how the world thinks about burnout

placemakes.label: Crying out for connection in a language the other person can't hear
placemakes.example: Like Sue Johnson discovering that couples fighting about dishes are actually screaming 'Are you there for me?' and building Emotionally Focused Therapy to translate the real conversation

placemakes.label: Suffering from something you've been trained not to name
placemakes.example: Like Terry Real writing I Don't Want to Talk About It, the first book to name male depression as a hidden epidemic that men are socialised to deny

categories.tagline: Ecological destruction, species loss, and climate crisis happening while most people look away
categories.turnsInto: Environmental consulting, sustainability coaching, regenerative design, climate communication

placemakes.label: The natural world being poisoned while governments look the other way
placemakes.example: Like Rachel Carson publishing Silent Spring while dying of cancer she kept secret, exposing DDT bioaccumulation the chemical industry had been hiding since the 1940s

placemakes.label: The climate crisis being treated as tomorrow's problem when it's already here
placemakes.example: Like Greta Thunberg saying 'I don't want you to be hopeful. I want you to panic. I want you to feel the fear I feel every day. And then I want you to act'

placemakes.label: Businesses profiting from nature while destroying it
placemakes.example: Like Yvon Chouinard transferring ownership of Patagonia to fight the climate crisis, saying 'Earth is now our only shareholder'

placemakes.label: Our language making it impossible to treat the natural world as alive
placemakes.example: Like Robin Wall Kimmerer noting that in Potawatomi 'to be a bay' is a verb, while in English 'we'd never call our grandmother it, yet we do so with every plant, tree, and river we meet'

categories.displayName: A life that isn't yours to live
categories.tagline: Systems of control that own, oppress, or decide your life for you
categories.turnsInto: Human rights advocacy, community organising, political leadership, legal reform, liberation work

placemakes.label: Your life being treated as someone else's asset
placemakes.example: Like Harriet Tubman escaping slavery and returning to the South roughly 13 times to guide approximately 70 enslaved people to freedom, with no record of her ever losing a passenger

placemakes.label: An entire population being dehumanized by law based on the colour of their skin
placemakes.example: Like Desmond Tutu spending decades confronting apartheid, from writing warnings to the Prime Minister to chairing the Truth and Reconciliation Commission

placemakes.label: The room getting quieter because everyone stopped pushing back
placemakes.example: Like Timothy Snyder noting 'Most of the power of authoritarianism is freely given. The Nazis did not have to demand compliance from most institutions. The institutions offered it'

placemakes.label: Ordinary people having no power against the institutions that run their lives
placemakes.example: Like Saul Alinsky building the modern template for community organising rooted in institutions people already belonged to, like parishes and unions, not abstract movements

placemakes.label: Being punished for being in pain
placemakes.example: Like Johann Hari travelling 30,000 miles across nine countries for Chasing the Scream and concluding that the opposite of addiction is not sobriety but connection

categories.tagline: Knowledge made unnecessarily hard, wrapped in jargon, or explained so badly you blame yourself
categories.turnsInto: Science communication, explainer content, courses, accessible publishing, translation

placemakes.label: Important knowledge buried behind jargon nobody can get through
placemakes.example: Like Randall Munroe using only the thousand most common English words to explain a Saturn V rocket, discovering he had to relearn things he thought he already understood

placemakes.label: The whole world being wrong about basic facts and nobody correcting them
placemakes.example: Like Hans Rosling showing audiences at Davos scored worse than random chance on global development questions: 'You are getting less than a chimpanzee. That is actively wrong ideas'

placemakes.label: Mathematics being taught so badly that people decide they're not smart enough
placemakes.example: Like Marcus du Sautoy saying 'No one teaches music by making children copy scales for eight years and then asks why no one wants to be a composer. That is how we teach maths'

placemakes.label: Being afraid to cook because nobody taught you the why, only the recipe
placemakes.example: Like Julia Child keeping mistakes in on live television so the viewer at home would believe they could do it too, treating the fear as the enemy, not the roux

placemakes.label: Tools built for the buyer, not the user
placemakes.example: Like Stewart Butterfield building Slack to feel human in a category that was grey and joyless, winning users bottom-up rather than through procurement departments

placemakes.label: Pretending you understand money because nobody taught you and you're too ashamed to ask
placemakes.example: Like Tiffany Aliche losing everything in a financial scam, then building The Budgetnista to teach money in the plain, warm voice she wished someone had used with her

categories.displayName: Locked out of what you need
categories.tagline: Education, healthcare, opportunity, or basic dignity blocked by cost, credentials, or gatekeeping
categories.turnsInto: Open-access platforms, scholarship programs, community education, social enterprise

placemakes.label: Education being out of reach for anyone who can't pay
placemakes.example: Like Sal Khan turning down multi-million-dollar offers and registering Khan Academy as a non-profit because 'I could not tell Nadia her tutoring was free and then charge her daughter'

placemakes.label: Being denied the right to learn because of who you are
placemakes.example: Like Malala Yousafzai blogging for BBC Urdu at age 11 describing life under Taliban rule, then being shot by the Taliban for it at 15

placemakes.label: Tools you need being too expensive or complicated for anyone without training
placemakes.example: Like Melanie Perkins pitching 100+ investors who said no, then building Canva to prove that design tools could work for everyone, not just professionals

placemakes.label: Talented people stuck in poverty because the doors are locked from outside
placemakes.example: Like Andrew Carnegie building 2,509 public libraries because he believed a library had changed his own life and could change anyone's

placemakes.label: A world built as if you don't exist
placemakes.example: Like Judith Heumann spending her childhood fighting for the right to attend public school in a wheelchair, then leading the 504 Sit-In that forced the US government to sign disability rights into law

categories.displayName: Your work being treated as nothing
categories.tagline: Art, craft, and creative vision being blocked, stolen, ignored, or treated as less than serious
categories.turnsInto: Creative coaching, art therapy, design leadership, creative entrepreneurship, artists' advocacy

placemakes.label: Being ahead of your time and dismissed for it
placemakes.example: Like Hilma af Klint producing the first fully abstract paintings in Western art around 1906, years before Kandinsky, then specifying they not be shown until 20 years after her death

placemakes.label: Being told your designs are impossible when the real issue is who drew them
placemakes.example: Like Zaha Hadid being dismissed as a 'paper architect' for sixteen years until the Vitra Fire Station proved the drawings could become buildings

placemakes.label: Choosing between making honest work and paying the rent
placemakes.example: Like Philip Glass driving a taxi and working as an unlicensed plumber until 41 so that his music would not have to pay the rent

placemakes.label: Someone else getting credit for what you built
placemakes.example: Like Nikola Tesla inventing alternating current while Edison took the credit, and Marconi receiving the Nobel for radio using Tesla's own patents

placemakes.label: Having to will yourself into existence because nobody makes room for you
placemakes.example: Like Octavia Butler writing in a 1988 notebook 'I shall be a bestselling writer,' working daytime jobs and writing at 2-3am because 'Forget inspiration. Habit is more dependable'

categories.tagline: People abandoned by systems built without them, falling through cracks nobody designed a net for
categories.turnsInto: Community building, social enterprise, disaster response, mutual aid, neighbourhood work, UX advocacy

placemakes.label: Being asked to prove you deserve the basics
placemakes.example: Like Dorothy Day's Houses of Hospitality offering food and shelter without intake forms, conditions or proselytising, with staff living alongside the people they served

placemakes.label: Being seen as your worst moment instead of your full self
placemakes.example: Like Hamdi Ulukaya buying a shuttered factory to build Chobani and hiring refugees because he saw workers, not charity cases

placemakes.label: Belonging nowhere after the thing that gave you purpose ends
placemakes.example: Like Sebastian Junger arguing that veterans' suffering is less about combat and more about returning to an individualist society, creating Vets Town Hall where veterans speak and civilians listen

placemakes.label: People going hungry in disasters because the relief system is slower than a kitchen
placemakes.example: Like Jose Andres founding World Central Kitchen, serving over 350 million meals in disaster zones worldwide, proving food could be the fastest first responder

placemakes.label: Cities built for cars and planners instead of the people who actually live there
placemakes.example: Like Jane Jacobs attacking the entire mid-century consensus from her apartment, then leading the fight that defeated Robert Moses's ten-lane expressway through Lower Manhattan

placemakes.label: Growing old in a building designed for efficiency instead of life
placemakes.example: Like Bill Thomas replacing fluorescent-lit nursing homes with the Eden Alternative, adding plants, animals, and children because loneliness kills faster than most diseases

placemakes.label: The only help available being designed for someone nothing like you
placemakes.example: Like Holly Whitaker building Tempest after realising recovery programmes designed for 1930s white men were the only option for a millennial woman in 2016

categories.displayName: Forgetting what it was all for
categories.tagline: The search for purpose, connection, and what makes a life worth living when the old answers stop working
categories.turnsInto: Life coaching, spiritual direction, philosophical counselling, retreat facilitation, meaning-making

placemakes.label: Losing everything and having to choose whether meaning still exists
placemakes.example: Like Viktor Frankl losing his wife, brother, and mother in the camps, then choosing to remain in Vienna and rebuild, applying his own theory of choosing attitude toward unchangeable facts

placemakes.label: Not being able to see your own life story as something that matters
placemakes.example: Like Joseph Campbell proposing the monomyth, a universal hero's journey underlying all cultures' myths, giving people a framework to understand their own path

placemakes.label: Your mind being your own worst enemy every morning before you even get out of bed
placemakes.example: Like Marcus Aurelius writing self-talk to get himself out of bed: 'I have to go to work, as a human being,' the earliest surviving written morning practice in Western literature

placemakes.label: Chasing winning so hard you forget to build the character that makes winning worth it
placemakes.example: Like John Wooden building the Pyramid of Success around character traits, not basketball skills, and telling players their career should read as a life first, a game second

placemakes.label: The most important things in life being the ones nobody teaches you
placemakes.example: Like Alain de Botton founding The School of Life because philosophy, love, work, and death are left out of every curriculum while algebra is mandatory

categories.tagline: The damage done when people stop questioning and start knowing, in science, politics, or daily life
categories.turnsInto: Critical thinking workshops, dialogue design, facilitation, systems thinking, decision advisory

placemakes.label: Absolute certainty turning people into the worst version of themselves
placemakes.example: Like Jacob Bronowski walking into the ash pond at Auschwitz and saying 'When people believe that they have absolute knowledge, with no test in reality, this is how they behave'

placemakes.label: Smart people making terrible decisions because they only use one lens
placemakes.example: Like Charlie Munger collecting mental models across psychology, physics, biology, and economics, arguing any single-discipline approach was guaranteed to produce blind spots

placemakes.label: Trying to control everything instead of learning to dance with it
placemakes.example: Like Donella Meadows writing 'mastery has less to do with pushing leverage points than with strategically, profoundly, madly letting go and dancing with the system'

placemakes.label: Fooling yourself and calling it science
placemakes.example: Like Richard Feynman saying 'The first principle is that you must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool,' defining integrity as leaning over backwards to show how you might be wrong

categories.tagline: Jobs that strip dignity, businesses that exploit, and systems that treat workers as disposable
categories.turnsInto: Workplace culture consulting, ethical business coaching, career transition, social entrepreneurship

placemakes.label: Watching someone you love be broken by their work
placemakes.example: Like Brunello Cucinelli saying 'I saw my father coming home offended, mortified' from the factory, then building a billion-dollar company while paying workers above market and mandating 90-minute lunches

placemakes.label: Doing a job that produces nothing and knowing it every single day
placemakes.example: Like David Graeber receiving thousands of emails from people describing their meaningless work: 'I did not intend to write a book. The readers wrote it for me'

placemakes.label: Being punished for doing the right thing
placemakes.example: Like James Sinegal telling analysts who called Costco's wages too high: 'Those are our core strengths, not problems,' holding the line on wages and low prices for decades

placemakes.label: Workers being treated as disposable by companies that couldn't function without them
placemakes.example: Like Howard Schultz growing up watching his father injured and uninsured in working-class jobs, then building Starbucks into the company his father never got a chance to work for
